question: What is the primary purpose of the Model for Improvement in healthcare?

options.A: To punish staff for poor clinical outcomes
options.B: To replace traditional nursing research entirely
options.C: To increase the paperwork burden on nurses
options.D: To guide rapid and meaningful clinical changes

explanation: The model provides a structured framework for nursing teams to implement fast, practical improvements in patient care units. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h1)

question: How does quality improvement using this model differ from traditional clinical research?

options.A: Research only happens in community health clinics
options.B: Research uses rapid testing instead of long studies
options.C: Quality improvement requires formal hospital ethics approval
options.D: Quality improvement focuses on local, rapid practice changes

explanation: While research proves broad theories over long periods, the Model for Improvement targets fast, practical changes within specific clinical settings. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three fundamental questions?

options.A: What are we trying to accomplish?
options.B: How will we know that a change is an improvement?
options.C: How much budget will this project require?
options.D: What change can we make that will result in improvement?

explanation: Budgeting is practical management, but the core framework relies strictly on aims, measures, and change ideas. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why must the three foundational questions be answered before starting a test?

options.A: To guarantee that the hospital receives extra government funding
options.B: To provide a clear direction and tracking method for the team
options.C: To satisfy strict regulatory licensing requirements for nurses
options.D: To determine which staff members will receive disciplinary action

explanation: Establishing clear aims, measures, and change concepts prevents confusion and keeps the nursing team focused on the goal. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h2)

question: A well-written aim statement must always include which of the following elements?

options.A: A specific time frame and measurable target
options.B: A list of nurses who failed previous shifts
options.C: A detailed breakdown of monthly nursing salaries
options.D: An approval signature from the hospital director

explanation: Clear aims need concrete numbers and deadlines so the team knows exactly what target they are working toward. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which statement represents the best clinical aim for a medical ward?

options.A: Decrease catheter-associated urinary tract infections by 50% over two months
options.B: Make sure our patients never get any hospital infections again
options.C: Tell patients to wash their hands more often during visiting hours
options.D: Improve nursing care standards across the entire hospital system

explanation: This option specifies a measurable clinical target and a clear timeline, making it actionable for the ward staff. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h3)

question: What do process measures track during a quality improvement project?

options.A: Whether clinical steps and interventions are performed correctly
options.B: Unintended negative consequences happening elsewhere in the unit
options.C: The total financial cost of supplies used during the shift
options.D: The ultimate health outcomes experienced by the patient

explanation: Process measures look at daily actions to ensure the new workflow or intervention is actually being executed as planned. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why do nursing teams track balancing measures during an improvement project?

options.A: To catch unintended problems created in other areas of the system
options.B: To calculate the exact financial profit generated by the new care plan
options.C: To make sure that every nurse works an equal number of night shifts
options.D: To replace the need for measuring patient clinical outcomes

explanation: Balancing measures act as a safety check to ensure fixing one problem does not accidentally create a new one elsewhere. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h4)

question: Where do effective change ideas typically originate in a clinical setting?

options.A: Patient complaints submitted directly to the board
options.B: Punitive policies written by hospital administrators
options.C: Random guesses made during morning handover meetings

explanation: Good change ideas come from studying current clinical processes and applying proven evidence to solve identified bottlenecks. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why is it important to select high-leverage changes rather than trying every idea at once?

options.A: It guarantees that no mistakes will ever occur on the ward
options.B: Hospital management forbids testing more than one idea
options.C: It prevents staff burnout and makes testing manageable
options.D: Patients will refuse care if too many changes happen

explanation: Focusing on manageable, high-impact ideas allows the nursing team to test changes without overwhelming daily clinical routines. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h5)

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle do nurses actually carry out the clinical test?
explanation: The 'Do' phase involves executing the planned change on a small scale and noting any problems that occur. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nursing team finishes running a small trial of a new handover checklist and compares the results to their prediction. Which PDSA phase are they performing?
explanation: Comparing data against predictions to evaluate success falls under the 'Study' phase of the cycle. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why should initial PDSA tests always be conducted on a very small scale?

options.A: To limit risk and make adjustments easy
options.B: To ensure patients never notice the nursing change
options.C: To hide the project from hospital inspectors
options.D: To reduce the amount of required documentation

explanation: Testing on a small scale protects patients and allows nurses to fix flaws quickly before rolling out a wider change. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h7)

question: When is it appropriate to spread a successful change across the entire hospital?

options.A: After consistent success across multiple small-scale PDSA tests
options.B: When the hospital budget requires spending extra money
options.C: As soon as the nursing director suggests a new idea
options.D: Immediately after the very first successful shift test

explanation: Scaling up requires confidence built from repeated successful tests under varying clinical conditions. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h7)
